included: One Pulse-owned identity module, packages/shared/src/productIdentity.ts, with a subpath export.
Desktop runtime identity: app user model id, URL schemes, Linux desktop entry and WM class, Electron user-data directory, home base dir.
Packaging identity in scripts/build-desktop-artifact.ts: appId, product name, artifact name, protocols, Linux executable and StartupWMClass, microphone string, DMG title.
Development launcher bundle id, display name and scheme.
Runbook for assembling and recording a Windows x64 installer.
excluded: Any Pulse update feed or publication.
Server CLI default home in apps/server/src/os-jank.ts, which stays T3's.
Worktree dev-home logic in packages/shared/src/devHome.ts, unchanged.
Renaming environment variables or adding PULSE_* aliases.

upstreamEdits: apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopEnvironment.ts: identity fields from the module; legacyUserDataDirName removed.
apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopAppIdentity.ts: legacy user-data lookup and its error type removed.
apps/desktop/scripts/electron-launcher.mjs: duplicated strings, launcher version bumped to 16.
Tests that pinned the old strings in apps/desktop/src and scripts.

acceptance.case: Packaged Windows config carries appId, productName and artifactName from the identity module.
acceptance.verification: scripts/build-desktop-artifact.test.ts, "packages under the Pulse Next identity, with no update feed by default".

acceptance.case: No publish config is emitted when neither T3CODE_DESKTOP_UPDATE_REPOSITORY nor GITHUB_REPOSITORY is set, so no app-update.yml ships and the updater reports no feed.
acceptance.verification: Same test asserts notProperty(config, "publish") for win and linux. DesktopUpdates.readAppUpdateYml maps a missing file to Option.none, and hasUpdateFeedConfig then disables automatic updates.

acceptance.case: The user data path never resolves to a T3 directory, even when %APPDATA%\t3code or "T3 Code (Alpha)" exists.
acceptance.verification: apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopAppIdentity.test.ts, "never adopts a T3 Code userData directory, even when one exists", with a FileSystem stub that reports every probed path as present.

acceptance.case: Base dir defaults to ~/.pulse-next for production and development.
acceptance.verification: apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopEnvironment.test.ts, production identity case and "keeps implicit development state separate from production state".

acceptance.case: An explicit T3CODE_HOME still wins over the default base dir.
acceptance.verification: apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopEnvironment.test.ts, explicit-home cases; apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopEarlyElectronStartup.test.ts for the pre-Electron path.

acceptance.case: Schemes pulsenext and pulsenext-dev are registered; no t3code scheme is registered or aliased.
acceptance.verification: apps/desktop/src/electron/ElectronProtocol.test.ts; protocols assertions in scripts/build-desktop-artifact.test.ts for mac and linux.

acceptance.case: Linux desktop entry, URL handler entry and WM class use the pulsenext names.
The development launcher bundle id stays under the Pulse Next namespace and keeps its per-repo suffix.
acceptance.verification: apps/desktop/scripts/electron-launcher.test.mjs, "repeats the shared product identity without drifting from it".

acceptance.case: An installer build on Windows x64 succeeds and installs beside T3 Code.
acceptance.verification: Reserved for the user. Not run by the implementation owner; see docs/operations/pulse-next-installer.md for the command and the hash recording step.

typecheck.baseline: packages/shared, apps/desktop and scripts all exit 0 at base; apps/desktop reports 4 pre-existing Effect suggestions.
typecheck.after: Unchanged: all three exit 0, same 4 suggestions in apps/desktop, no new errors.

limitations: The packaged app still carries T3's icon. The export pipeline needs macOS-only ictool and an Icon Composer project, and no Pulse artwork exists in the repository.

The WSL backend still caches its Linux runtime at $HOME/.t3/wsl-runtime inside the WSL distro, which a T3 Code install would share. That cache is keyed by version and architecture and holds no user data.
